Houston Texans|Buffalo Bills.read: The model has Houston -3.5 while the market has Buffalo -1.5, a 5-point gap, yet nothing on the injury sheet explains it: Houston is full strength and Buffalo's three questionable tags net to roughly -0.02 after backups, so the entire disagreement lives in the base power ratings (Houston 3.65 vs Buffalo 2.13 plus 2 HFA). Under Walters' framework, when the market disagrees with your number by a full touchdown-range swing and you cannot point to availability information they lack, the presumption is that your ratings have drifted, not that the market has erred. The unit-level data doesn't rescue the model either: both teams grade similarly weak in protection and Buffalo actually holds the rushing edge, so there is no matchup story supporting a Texans-by-a-field-goal line. The 1-star rating (8.5%) is correctly flagging low conviction despite the large nominal gap. Absent a concrete reason the market is wrong, this is noise, and the right play is to pass and re-examine the Buffalo/Houston ratings rather than fade a road favorite the market clearly believes in.
Houston Texans|Buffalo Bills.risks: If the Buffalo rating is genuinely stale and Houston is being undervalued, the home side has value, but betting on that without a driver is guessing; the 1-point total gap (45.5 vs 44.5) is well inside normal error and offers no edge.
